Scheme Name: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture
Assistance: 1) Area expansion / new orchards for mango, guava, aonla, litchi, citrus, banana, papaya, strawberry, dragon fruit, etc. Assistance provided as per MIDH norms (capital cost support for planting material + cultivation costs for 2 years; capped per ha/beneficiary)  2) Rejuvenation / canopy management of old and senile orchards.  3) Vegetable / spice area expansion – hybrid vegetables, onion, garlic, chillies, turmeric, etc.  4) Area expansion under flowers, medicinal & aromatic plants  5) Protected cultivation – polyhouse, shade-net house, low tunnels, mulching, anti-hail/bird nets etc.  6) As per revised MIDH norms: ~50% subsidy of admissible cost for general states; area caps per beneficiary.  7) UP has additionally announced up to 50% subsidy for polyhouse/greenhouse construction leveraging MIDH and AIF.  8) Bee-keeping (apiculture) – supply of bee colonies, boxes, equipment under MIDH/National Bee Board. 9)  Post-harvest & marketing infrastructure – pack houses, pre-cooling units, cold rooms, reefer vans, onion storage, ripening chambers, minimal processing units, etc.  10) HRD & extension – farmer trainings, exposure visits, demonstrations.  11) Mechanization – small tractor, power tillers, etc.  12) Support for additional components such as fencing, support system (मचान), fruit bags, etc.
Eligibility: 1) Individual farmers (priority: small & marginal, women, SC/ST, OBC) FPOs/FPCs, SHGs, cooperatives.  2) Farmer groups/Companies (for project-based components like cold storage, pack houses, etc.)  3) Applicant shall possess the title or registered lease of the horticulture land against which scheme benefit has been applied for Minimum and maximum area limits vary across components.   4) Up to 2 ha per beneficiary in case of area expansion / orchards.  5) Area varies across ~2,500–4,000 sq.m per beneficiary, depending on structure, in case of protected cultivation.  6) Cold storages up to a capacity of 5000 MT
Contact Point: District Horticulture Officer (DHO)

Scheme Name: Uttar Pradesh Food Processing Industry Policy
Assistance:
Capital Subsidy
For new food-processing units (FPIs): up to 35% subsidy of incurred expenditure on plant & machinery, technical civil work subject to a maximum of ₹5 crore.
For expansion/modernisation/up-gradation: 25% subsidy, subject to a maximum of ₹1 crore.
Promotion of decentralized processing and storage:
SHGs/FPOs/Framers will be eligible for assistance in this form of grant
Maximum limit of 50% of the total project cost or Rs. 50 lacs.
Land & Land-use Incentives
Permission to purchase agricultural land for FPIs beyond 12.5 acres.
Exemption from fees @2% of the value at circle rate on non-agricultural use declaration for FPIs.
100% exemption from stamp duty on land purchased for establishment of food processing industry
Exemption from fees for exchange of government-owned land coming under project site.
50% waiver in Conversion of Land Use (CLU) fees
Mandi‐Fee / Cess Exemptions
Exemption from mandi fees and cess for agricultural produce procured from other states for processing in UP as well as for agricultural produce directly sold to processing units by farmers in UP
Cold-Chain / Value Addition / Infrastructure Support
Subsidy of 35% for infrastructure related to cold chain & value addition. For frozen storage / deep freezers / value-addition/processing infrastructure, subsidy up to 50% subject to a maximum up to ₹10 crore
For Agro Processing Clusters: minimum 5 food processing units with minimum investment of ₹25 crore → grant of 35% of project cost subject to maximum ₹10 crore.
Interest subsidy on purchase of reefer vehicles / mobile pre-cooling vans, reimbursed for five years to a maximum limit ~₹50 lakh.
Solar Power/Green Energy Incentives
Subsidy for solar power projects for electricity supply to processing units in rural areas: 50% subsidy, for women entrepreneurs in same category subsidy is 90%
Other Incentives
Freight subsidy: 25% on exports (excluding Nepal, Bangladesh and Bhutan).
Support for modern technology adoption to food-processing start-ups in agriculture value-chain development up to ~₹5 crore.
Rebate of 75% on External Development Charges (EDC) for FPI.
Eligibility:
Food Processing Industry (FPI) is defined broadly: enterprises involved in transformation of raw agricultural/horticultural/animal products or further value addition of food items.
Eligible units include: new units, expansion/modernisation/upgrade of existing units; setting up of value-addition, cold-chain, storage facilities, pack-house, etc.
For the subsidy: The unit must be located in UP, registered, meet required standards (plant & machinery, technical civil works) and eligible cost norms.
There may be minimum investment/expenditure thresholds for certain components (e.g., clusters – min investment ₹25 crore) as cited above.
The policy does not restrict only to large units; smaller units in FPI sector are eligible for subsidy proportionally, subject to cost incurred and caps (e.g., ₹5 crore cap for subsidy for new units).
Units must comply with regulatory requirements (land use conversion, environmental clearance, building permits, fire safety, labour regulations, food safety standards).
Beneficiaries must submit applications through the state nodal portal (Invest UP / DOHFP) and abide by the conditions for subsidy disbursement (often after verification, project completion).
Contact Point: District Industries Centre (DIC)

Scheme Name: Uttar Pradesh Matsya Palak Kalyan Kosh Yojana (Training & Welfare Fund)
Assistance:
(A) Assistance for Natural Calamity Loss (दैवीय आपदा सहायता)
Financial assistance to fish farmer / fisherman families for damage or loss caused by natural calamities (floods, heavy rains, etc.) affecting ponds, nets, boats, gear, or stock.
Objective: Quick livelihood restoration so that families can resume fish culture/fishing without falling into chronic debt. 
(B) Medical Assistance (चिकित्सा सहायता)
Financial support to fish farmers/fishermen and their family members in case of serious illness or accidental injury.
Objective: Reduce health-related financial shocks in highly vulnerable fishing households. 
(C) Training, Exposure Visits and Seminars (प्रशिक्षण / भ्रमण / सेमिनार)
Support for inter-state and intra-state exposure visits, skill development trainings, exhibitions, seminars for fishers and fish farmers.
Includes:
Technical training on modern aquaculture, seed production, feed management, disease control, etc.
Exposure to successful fisheries/aquaculture projects in other states
(D) Fisher Housing with Single Dwelling (मछुआ आवास निर्माण सहायता)
Graded financial assistance for construction of a fisherman’s house with single dwelling as per area and cost norms notified by the State Government.
Objective: Provide dignified housing to eligible fishers in fish-dominated villages.
(E) Community Centre Support (सामुदायिक केंद्र सहायता)
Assistance from the fund for construction or up-gradation of community centres in villages with high fisher populations, to be used for community meetings, training sessions, storage, or small-scale processing/marketing activities.
(F) Infrastructure & Demonstration Centre Renovation (Recent amendment)
Recent orders have allowed the fund to also be used for renovation and redevelopment of departmental “प्रेक्षेत्र” (demonstration fields/centres) and other fisheries infrastructure in fish-dominated villages, beyond earlier village-level development activities. 
(G) Other notified sub-projects
Communication from districts for FY 2025-26 additionally mention:
Moped with Ice Box (mobile fish vending) and
Expanded training and exposure programmes implemented “under the Uttar Pradesh Matsya Palak Kalyan Kosh”.
Eligibility:
Fish farmers and fishermen (मत्स्य पालक / मछुआ) and their families who are:
Engaged in fish business or fisheries activities and
Using fisheries/aquaculture as their primary livelihood for at least one year or more.
Traditional riverine fishing communities, including केवट, मल्लाह, निषाद, बिन्द, धीमर, कश्यप, बाथम, रैकवार, मांझी, गोडिया, कहार, तुरैहा/तुराहा and other similar communities customarily engaged in fishing.
Fishers and fish farmers in “मत्स्य पालक बहुल ग्राम” (villages with high concentration of fishers), particularly to support local infrastructure and community assets
Fulfil specific criteria of the relevant sub-component, as for instance examples have been outlined below:
For calamity loss assistance – proof of loss due to notified calamity and verification by local officers. 
For medical assistance – documentation of illness, hospitalisation, costs, etc.
For training/exposure – being an active fish farmer/fisher nominated by District Fisheries Officer. 
For housing / community centre – availability of land/plot as per norms; location in fish-dominated area; priority to vulnerable groups.

(3) Group-based eligibility: SHGs are typically 10–15 women (or 5–20 in special cases); eligibility for revolving fund, community investment fund, interest subvention is linked to group grading, regular savings, meetings, and internal lending practices.

Contact Point: Chief Development Officer (CDO), District Agriculture Officer (DAO)

Department: UTTAR PRADESH DIVERSIFIED AGRICULTURE SUPPORT PROJECT

Assistance:

Contact Point: Chief Development Officer (CDO), District Agriculture Officer (DAO)

Department: UTTAR PRADESH DIVERSIFIED AGRICULTURE SUPPORT PROJECT

Assistance:
(1) FPO formation & incubation support through CBBOs for 5 years (mobilisation, registration, business planning, governance training).

Contact Point: Chief Development Officer (CDO)

Department: UTTAR PRADESH DIVERSIFIED AGRICULTURE SUPPORT PROJECT
Scheme Name: Public–Private Partnership for Agriculture Value Chain Development Programme
Assistance:
(1) PPPAVCD organises and targets other scheme benefits into PPP clusters. The broad areas of the support extended under programme are outlined:
(a) Inputs & productivity support
(b) Quality seed / hybrids, minikits – via NFSM / RKVY / State seed schemes.
(c) Soil health, micronutrients, bio-fertilisers – via NMSA / SHC / PKVY.
(d) On-farm infrastructure & equipment
(e) Micro-irrigation and water-use efficiency – via PMKSY.
(f) Farm mechanisation (planters, harvesters, dryers) – via SMAM, RKVY, State mechanisation schemes.
(g) Post-harvest & value-chain infrastructure
(h) Godowns, pack-houses, cold rooms – via Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) and state warehouse schemes.
(i) Primary processing units and small agro-processing – via PMFME, MIDH, RKVY – marketing components.
(j) Financial support: Interest subvention, credit guarantees, blended finance – via AIF / NABARD / CGTMSE-linked products.
(k) Technology & agronomy support – private partner gives structured PoP, training, precision tools. 
(l) Market assurance – cluster-level buy-back contracts or procurement commitments (e.g. Ninjacart, distilleries). 
(m) Risk reduction – diversification, improved agronomy, offtake stability, plus insurance via PMFBY where applicable.
Eligibility:
(1) Primary beneficiary: 
(a) Small and marginal farmers in PPPAVCD clusters (crop + geography defined in each project). 
(b) FPOs / FPGs / Cooperatives / SHG federations engaged as aggregation and implementation arms.
(2) Secondary beneficiary: 
(a) Private companies / start-ups / agribusinesses selected as PPP partners.
(b) MSMEs in the value chain (transporters, input dealers, processors).
(c) Financial institutions lending into the cluster, supported by interest subvention / guarantees via converged schemes like AIF.
(3) Farmer eligibility: 
(a) Farmer must be within the notified cluster villages/blocks of an approved PPPAVCD project.
(b) Preferably small/marginal, though larger farmers may be included to reach the 500–10,000 farmer envelope.
(c) Agree to:
(d) follow the package of practices laid out in the PPP (e.g. maize hybrid, fertigation regime),
(e) supply produce through FPO/cluster channels to the offtaker, and
(f) share basic data (area, yields, bank details) for DBT and monitoring.
(g) Aadhaar-linked bank account and KYC completed as per converged scheme rules.
(4) Private partner eligibility: 
(a) Registered company / LLP / eligible producer organisation with demonstrated value-chain experience.
(b) Strong balance sheet / solvency, proven offtake capacity (e.g. distillery, processor, retailer, e-commerce, logistics platform).
(c) Willingness to invest in on-ground systems, commit buy-back quantities, and share project-level data for central monitoring.
Contact Point: Chief Development Officer (CDO)

Department: UTTAR PRADESH DIVERSIFIED AGRICULTURE SUPPORT PROJECT
Scheme Name: Aatma Nirbhar Krishak Samnvita Vikas Yojna
Assistance:
(1) Support for formation and promotion of FPOs beyond the central scheme allocations
(2) Management / handholding support through empanelled CBBOs similar to 10k FPO scheme.
(3) State-level budget for:
(a) Capacity-building, business plan preparation and market linkages.
(b) Support for infrastructure and working capital
Eligibility:
(1) Farmer groups organised into FPOs/Producer Companies/Cooperatives in clusters identified by GoUP/UPDASP.
(2) Focus on small & marginal farmers and commodities important for state diversification (pulses, oilseeds, horticulture, dairy, fisheries etc.).
Contact Point: Chief Development Officer (CDO)

Department: UTTAR PRADESH DIVERSIFIED AGRICULTURE SUPPORT PROJECT
Scheme Name: Uttar Pradesh Agriculture Growth and Rural Enterprise Ecosystem Strengthening Project
Assistance:
(1) To increase farmers’ income through improved crop productivity, climate resilience, and commercialization of agrifood systems in selected regions of state i.e. 28 districts across Jhansi, Chitrakoot, Vindhyachal, Varanasi, Gorakhpur, Azamgarh, Basti, and Devipatan divisions.
(2) Improve climate-resilient productivity of key crops (rice, wheat, maize, gram, mustard, etc.) in the project districts.
(3) Develop competitive, inclusive value chains for prioritized commodities (crops, horticulture, livestock, fisheries) through clusters and agribusiness investments.
(4) Strengthen digital and financial ecosystems (Agri-stack, UP AGRIVERSE, digital KCC / credit, AIF-type funds) for farmers, FPOs and agri-MSMEs.
(5) Leverage private capital for agrifood MSMEs and value-chain investments.
(6) Enhance institutional capacity of GoUP, UPDASP and district systems for climate-smart agriculture, value-chain development, and monitoring / learning.
Eligibility:
(1) Primary beneficiary:
(a)	Small and marginal farmers, including women farmers and tenant / sharecroppers where allowed by project rules.
(b)	Farmer Producer Groups (FPGs) and Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs / FPCs).
(c)	Fishers and fish farmers in project blocks (for fisheries and aquaculture sub-projects).
(d)	Agri-MSMEs and start-ups in input, post-harvest, processing, logistics and services.
(e)	Women-led and youth-led enterprises in agrifood systems.
(2) Secondary beneficiary:
(a)	Farmer families accessing improved digital services (advisory, scheme access, grievance, etc.).
(b)	Banks, NBFCs, MFIs participating in the digital credit and AIF platforms.
(c)	Research / technical agencies (SAUs, ICAR institutes, KVKs) partnering for climate-resilient practices.
(3) Broad eligibility criteria:
(a)	The farmer / group / enterprise must be located in a notified project district / block and within a project commodity cluster, where applicable.
(b)	The farmer should be registered in the state’s agriculture database / UP AGRIVERSE (once operational) with valid Aadhaar-linked bank account and land / lease details, as per project guidelines.
(c)	FPGs / FPOs / SHGs / CLFs / cooperatives must be legally registered entities (Societies / Producer Companies / Cooperatives, etc.) and comply with UPAGREES eligibility norms for each component (e.g., minimum member base, audited accounts, business plan).
(d)	Agri-MSMEs must meet GoI/GoUP MSME definition, operate in the agrifood value chain, and satisfy the credit and due-diligence requirements of the AIF / bank / fund manager.
(e)	Beneficiaries must agree to follow environmental and social safeguards, including land, water and biodiversity norms prescribed in the ESMF / ESMP.
Contact Point: Chief Development Officer (CDO)

Assistance:
(1) Financial support from Government of India for creation of village water supply infrastructure such as source development/augmentation, water treatment units, overhead tanks, pumping systems, distribution pipelines, and household tap connections.
(2) Support for greywater management, source sustainability (rainwater harvesting, recharge structures), and water quality surveillance including field test kits and laboratories. 
(3) Capacity building and IEC (Information, Education & Communication) for behaviour change, community mobilisation, and training of Village Water & Sanitation Committees (VWSCs)/Pani Samitis, engineers, and local masons/plumbers.
Eligibility:
(1) All rural households (HHs) in all villages of India are eligible for Functional Household Tap Connections under JJM, with special focus on aspirational districts, quality affected habitations (e.g. arsenic/fluoride), drought prone, desert, tribal and difficult areas.

(3) There is no income-based exclusion at household level. However, schemes are planned at village/habitation level and implemented in a phased manner as per State Annual Action Plans.
Contact Point: District Water & Sanitation Mission (DWSM) office

Department: YUVA KALYAN AND PRANTIYA RAKSHAK DAL

Department: YUVA KALYAN AND PRANTIYA RAKSHAK DAL
Scheme Name: Prantiya Rakshak Dal (PRD) Volunteer Engagement Programme
Assistance:
(1) Enrolment of eligible rural youth as PRD jawans with basic training in drill, disaster response, traffic control, and crowd management.

Department: DIRECTORATE OF AGRICULTURAL MARKETING & AGRICULTURE FOREIGN TRADE
Scheme Name: Agricultural Marketing Intelligence & e NAM (Market Information + Online Trading)
Assistance:
(1) 211 Marketing Intelligence Centres across 251 regulated mandis and 371 sub mandis in UP collect daily data on arrivals, wholesale prices, stocks and movement.
(2) Daily and weekly wholesale prices are sent to All India Radio and Doordarshan. Analytical reports (weekly/fortnightly/monthly) are shared with State and Central departments for policy.
(3) Computerisation of 242 mandi nodes under AGMARKNET with NIC support; data from all revenue districts and key market centres is uploaded to www.agmarknet.nic.in 
(4) Farmers can see which market is offering better prices and decide where to sell.
(5) Integration with e NAM: 162 mandis of UP linked to www.enam.gov.in, where electronic auction and online bidding take place.
Eligibility:
(1) All farmers, FPOs and traders using UP mandis can use price/arrival information (no formal registration needed).
(2) For e NAM trading, farmer/FPO/trader must register on the e NAM portal or through the local mandi.
Contact Point: Mandi Secretary / Senior Agriculture Marketing Inspector

Department: DIRECTORATE OF AGRICULTURAL MARKETING & AGRICULTURE FOREIGN TRADE
Scheme Name: Assaying, Grading & Quality Management (including AGMARK & e NAM Labs)
Assistance:
(1) Grading units established in selected mandis (125 e-NAM mandis doing grading of ~247 commodities as per DMI’s tradable parameters).
(2) Assaying laboratories set up in 125 e-NAM mandis; Directorate has appointed trained assaying inspectors (trained by Government of India’s Directorate of Marketing & Inspection).
(3) In e-NAM:
(a) Mandi staff create lots from arriving produce.
(b) Assaying inspector draws samples as per protocol and determines grade in the lab.
(c) Grade and parameters are uploaded in the system. Buyers anywhere can see quality details before bidding.
(4) AGMARK grading for consumer level products:
(a) “AGMARK” is a quality mark for items like wheat flour, maida, suji, pulses, spices, ghee, oils, honey, tamarind, fruits, eggs etc.
(b) State AGMARK laboratories established in selected districts to expand grading and protect consumers against adulteration.
Eligibility:
(1) Farmers and traders bringing produce to e NAM mandis automatically covered for grading/assaying.
(2) Packers/processors who seek AGMARK grading and certification for retail products apply through DMI and state labs.
Contact Point: District level AGMARK Lab (where available) and Marketing Officer

Department: DIRECTORATE OF AGRICULTURAL MARKETING & AGRICULTURE FOREIGN TRADE
Scheme Name: Uttar Pradesh Agriculture Export Policy 2019 & Export Promotion Schemes
Assistance:
(1) Additional incentives for export-oriented clusters – support to identified product clusters (e.g. rice, mango, etc.) for infrastructure, branding and market linkages.

Eligibility:

(2) Institutions running approved export related courses, as notified.
Contact Point: Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) nodal officer

Eligibility:

Contact Point: Office of Chairman, District Ganga Committee

Assistance:

Scheme Name: Finance Commission Grants to Panchayats (Central & State)
Assistance:
(1) Tied grants for specific sectors (e.g., drinking water and sanitation under 15th FC).

Contact Point: District Panchayat Raj Officer (DPRO), District Nodal Officer RGSA

Assistance:
(1) Financial assistance for construction of a standard Panchayat Bhawan building.

Assistance:
(1) Individual Household Latrine (IHHL) Incentive: Central incentive of ₹12,000 per eligible rural household for constructing toilets, with flexibility for additional State share. Eligible categories include BPL and specified poor APL households (SC/ST, small/marginal farmers, landless labourers with homestead, persons with disabilities, women headed households).
(2) Community Sanitary Complexes (CSCs): Financial assistance to Gram Panchayats for constructing and maintaining CSCs where household toilets are difficult (e.g., land constraints, public places). 
(3) SLWM Infrastructure: Support for village level systems such as compost pits, soak pits, drainage, waste collection and treatment infrastructure, including faecal sludge treatment where applicable, to achieve ODF Plus status. 
(4) IEC & Capacity Building: Funds for Information Education Communication (IEC), Behaviour Change Communication (BCC), triggering exercises, and training of Swachhagrahis, VWSCs and PRI representatives.

Contact Point: District Panchayat Raj Officer (DPRO), District Nodal Officer RGSA

Contact Point: District Panchayat Raj Officer (DPRO), District Nodal Officer RGSA

Contact Point: District Panchayat Raj Officer (DPRO), District Nodal Officer RGSA

Assistance:
(1) Fund construction or renovation of school rooms, libraries, community halls, sports complexes, and Anganwadi centers.
(2) Support installation of solar lights, CCTV, water systems, and waste management.
(3) Contribute to beautification of ponds and public spaces.
Eligibility:
(1) Individuals: Permanent residents of Uttar Pradesh, including those living outside the state or abroad (NRI/PIO).

Contact Point: District Panchayat Raj Officer (DPRO), District Nodal Officer RGSA

Assistance:
(1) Technical and financial assistance for creation of new irrigation borings/tubewells of approved depths (e.g., shallow and medium deep) under the scheme. 
(2) Department provides boring services through empanelled agencies/departmental machinery and extends subsidy/assistance as per sanctioned unit cost and farmer category (e.g., higher benefit for small, marginal, SC/ST farmers). 
(3) Scheme is implemented through online application, selection and monitoring via MIU Online, improving transparency and time bound processing.
Eligibility:
(1) Eligible beneficiaries: Farmers of Uttar Pradesh owning cultivable land in notified blocks and fulfilling eligibility conditions (with prioritisation typically for small/marginal farmers; some districts separately list SC/ST or land holding criteria).
(2) Land and technical conditions: Sufficient land available for siting a boring/tubewell as per departmental spacing and safety norms. Site lies in a block/area permitted for new groundwater structures as per departmental and groundwater regulations.
Contact Point: Executive Engineer / District Minor Irrigation Officer (DMI/EE, Minor Irrigation)

Assistance:
(1) Department undertakes boring up to a prescribed depth (e.g., 110 mm dia up to about 30 m for shallow wells) at no cost to the eligible farmer; cost is borne from the scheme budget.
(2) In some districts, a per boring financial ceiling is notified (e.g., assistance up to ₹10,000 per boring for eligible SC BPL small/marginal farmers in plain areas).
(3) Materials and technical services (boring labour, casing, etc.) are provided as per departmental specifications; farmers arrange pump sets and ancillary works beyond the scheme scope.
Eligibility:
(1) Eligibility conditions are defined in state level guidelines and implemented uniformly, with district level notices giving details. Common elements are:
(a) Category: Small and marginal farmers, with special focus on Scheduled Caste families living below poverty line in plain areas; some GOs extend coverage to other poor small/marginal farmers as notified.
(b) Land holding: Minimum cultivable land (often 0.2 ha for general small/marginal farmers; this minimum may not apply to SC/ST small/marginal farmers as per guideline extract).
(c) Location conditions: Site should satisfy groundwater siting norms (e.g., minimum distance from existing borewells, block not in critical/over exploited category as per state orders).
Contact Point: Executive Engineer / District Minor Irrigation Officer (DMI/EE, Minor Irrigation)

Scheme Name: SILK SAMAGRA–2: Integrated Scheme for Development of Silk Industry (2021–2026)

The scheme offers comprehensive, multi-level support to farmers, SHGs, FPOs, reelers, and silk workers.
(1) Financial Assistance
(a) Subsidy for Rearing Sheds
(a.1) Up to 80% subsidy depending on category
(a.2) SC/ST beneficiaries get higher subsidy (up to 90%)
(2) Subsidy for Mulberry Plantation
(a) Support for land preparation, saplings, irrigation, inputs.
(3) Equipment Subsidy
(a) Rearing kits, mountages, disinfectants, tools, reeling equipment.
(4) Support for Chawki Rearing Centres (CRCs)
(a) Low-cost chawki silkworm supply to farmers.
(5) Credit-Linked Incentives
(a) Loan + subsidy combination for sheds, plantations, machines.
(6) Technical Assistance
(a) Training in mulberry cultivation, silkworm rearing, disease management, grainage operations.
(b) Quality improvement support (grading, testing, certification).
(c) Support from CSB scientists, district officers, and master trainers.
(6) Infrastructure Support
(a) 50,000 new rearing sheds
(b) 200 new CRCs
(c) Modernization of 500 grainages
(d) New quality and testing labs
(e) Improved reeling units & post-cocoon technology
(7) Women Empowerment Support
(a) Through Resham Sakhi Yojana:
(a.1) 100% free residential training
(a.2) 80% subsidy on rearing kits
(a.3) Home-based rearing opportunities
(a.4) Market linkage and group formation
(8) Market and Digital Support
(a) Access to cocoon markets, aggregators, and online auction platforms.
(b) SILKS 2.0 portal for real-time tracking.
(c) AI-based disease alerts and advisory.
Eligibility:
(1) Who can apply?
(a) Farmers
(a.1) Mulberry, Tasar, Eri, or Muga farmers
(a.2) Land-owning, tenant, or lease-holding farmers
(a.3) Priority to marginal farmers (up to 2 acres)
(2) SC/ST Communities
(a) Minimum 30% reservation in all components
(b) Additional subsidy support
(3) Women / SHGs / NRLM Groups
(a) Women interested in home-based silk activities
(b) Eligible for Resham Sakhi training and support
(4) FPOs / Cooperatives
(a) Can apply for group sheds, CRCs, reeling units
(5) Landless Individuals
(a) Eligible under group rearing sheds and post-cocoon employment
(6) Youth, Entrepreneurs, Small Industries
(a) Eligible for reeling, twisting, dyeing, and processing units
(7) Documents required:
(a) Aadhaar
(b) Bank account

Assistance:
The scheme provides a complete financial package covering all plantation establishment costs for the first 3 years (establishment + maintenance).
Total support includes Rs. 14,000 per acre for new plantation plus Rs. 4,500 per acre per year for maintenance during Years 2–3.
(1) New Plantation Development – Rs. 14,000 per acre
This is a complete package covering all initial establishment costs with the following detailed breakup:
(a) High-Quality Saplings: 500 plants per acre @ Rs. 2 per plant, total cost Rs. 1,000.
Improved varieties such as S-54, S-1635, AR-5 supplied from government nurseries.
(b) Farm Yard Manure (FYM): 10–15 tonnes @ Rs. 200 per tonne, total cost Rs. 3,000.
Used as organic manure to improve soil fertility.
(c) Chemical Fertilizers (NPK): Soil test–based application costing Rs. 3,500.
Ensures balanced nutrition during the first year.
(d) Pesticides / Insecticides: Six-month supply costing Rs. 1,500.
Protection against mealy bug and stem borer.
(e) Land Preparation Labor: Ploughing and leveling costing Rs. 2,000.
Includes tractor operations and manual labor.
(f) Planting Labor: Digging pits and planting costing Rs. 2,000.
Skilled labor ensures proper spacing and planting.
(g) Soil Conservation Measures: Mulching and bunding costing Rs. 1,000. Helps in water retention and erosion control.
(h) Total New Plantation Package Cost: Rs. 14,000 per acre.

(2) Subsidy Pattern for New Plantation
(a) General States (Uttar Pradesh): 50% CSB subsidy (Rs. 7,000) + 25% State share (Rs. 3,500) + 25% Farmer share (Rs. 3,500).
(b) Special States: 80% CSB subsidy (Rs. 11,200) + 10% State share (Rs. 1,400) + 10% Farmer share (Rs. 1,400).
(c) SC / ST / Women Beneficiaries: 65% CSB subsidy (Rs. 9,100) + 25% State share (Rs. 3,500) + 10% Farmer share (Rs. 1,400).

(3) Plantation Maintenance Support (Years 2–3)
(a) Support of Rs. 4,500 per acre per year is provided for maintenance activities.
(b) Maintenance package includes:
(b.1) Fertilizer Top-Dressing: Rs. 2,000 for NPK application to support growth.
(b.2) Pest Management: Rs. 800 for 8–10 sprays per season.
(b.3) Pruning Labor: Rs. 1,000 for four prunings per year.
(b.4) Weed Control: Rs. 500 for manual weeding and herbicide use.
(b.5) Mulching: Rs. 200 for moisture conservation.
(b.6) Total Maintenance Cost: Rs. 4,500 per acre per year.
(c) Maintenance Subsidy Pattern: Same as new plantation, i.e., 50% CSB + 25% State + 25% Farmer for Uttar Pradesh.

(4) Additional Technical Support (Provided Free of Cost)
(a) Sapling Quality Assurance: All saplings supplied from CSB-approved government or private nurseries with disease-free certification.
(b) Soil Testing: Free soil testing conducted at the district laboratory with customized fertilizer recommendations.
(c) Planting Guidance: Extension officers demonstrate correct planting techniques and spacing.
(d) Disease Management Advisory: Free technical advisory support during the first two years.
(e) Pruning Training: One-day hands-on pruning training provided free of cost.

(5) Irrigation Convergence Support (Additional Rs. 25,000–30,000 per acre)
(a) Drip Irrigation Package (Most Recommended):
(a.1) Unit cost: Rs. 30,000 per acre.
(a.2) Subsidy: 50% subsidy amounting to Rs. 15,000 free.
(b) Drip Package Includes:
(b.1) Main and sub-main pipes costing Rs. 12,000.
(b.2) Lateral pipes and drippers costing Rs. 8,000.
(b.3) Installation labor costing Rs. 6,000.
(b.4) Moisture sensors costing Rs. 4,000 (optional).
(c) Benefits: Water savings of 40–50% and yield increase of 20–25%.

(6) Farm Pond (Community-Based Irrigation):
(a) Capacity: 40 lakh liters (15 m × 15 m × 1.8 m).
(b) Total cost: Rs. 3 lakh.
(c) Subsidy: 50% subsidy amounting to Rs. 1.5 lakh free.
(d) Coverage: Serves 4–5 farmers cultivating approximately 0.5 acre each.

Assistance:
Resham Sakhi Yojana provides complete end-to-end support from training to market linkage, ensuring zero barriers for rural women to start silk production.

(1) All assistance under the scheme is 100% free or heavily subsidized.

(2) Free Residential Training (Core Assistance – 100% Free)
(a) Mulberry Silk Training
(a.1) Training Location - Central Sericulture Research & Training Institute, Mysore, Karnataka, which is a national center of excellence.
(a.2) Training Duration - 15–21 days as a full residential training program.
(a.3) Training Coverage - The training is 100% free and includes second-class train or bus travel, accommodation, food (three meals per day plus snacks), training materials, and certification.
(a.4) Training Content - Training covers mulberry cultivation, silkworm egg handling, disease prevention, maintenance of optimal rearing conditions, cocoon harvesting, and quality grading.
(a.5) Certification - An official government certificate is issued, which enhances market credibility.

(b) Tassar Silk Training
(b.1) Training Location - Central Tasar Research & Training Institute, Ranchi, Jharkhand.
(b.2) Training Duration - 15–21 days residential training.
(b.3) Training Coverage - 100% free training including travel, stay, food, and training materials.
(b.4) Training Content - Training includes tassar host plant management (Arjun and Sal trees), wild silkworm rearing, forest-based silk production, and tribal techniques adapted for home-based use.
(b.5) Certification - Official tassar silk expert certificate is provided.

(c) Local Awareness Training
(c.1) Training Location - District Sericulture Training Centers.
(c.2) Training Duration - 5–10 days non-residential training.
(c.3) Training Coverage - Free training along with a daily stipend of Rs. 200.
(c.4) Training Content - Basic silk production knowledge, business planning, and financial literacy.

(3) Financial and Infrastructure Support
(a) Home-Based Rearing Unit Setup
(a.1) Space Requirement - 100–200 square feet; veranda, small room, or balcony is sufficient.
(a.2) Rearing Kit Subsidy - Total kit cost is Rs. 20,000, with 80% subsidy. Rs. 16,000 is provided free, and the beneficiary contribution is Rs. 4,000.
(a.3) Kit Contents - Bamboo rearing trays (20) for silkworm bedding, Plastic rearing stands (4 sets) to organize trays, Mountages or cocoon frames (50) for silkworm spinning, Disinfection sprayer (1) for disease prevention, Leaf cutting tools (1 set) for mulberry leaf preparation, Weighing scale (1) for cocoon measurement, Thermometer and hygrometer (1 set) for temperature and humidity monitoring, and Training manuals (2 copies) as reference guides.

(b) Raw Material Support (First 1–2 Seasons)
(b.1) Silkworm Eggs - Free first batch of Disease Free Layings (DFLs) ranging from 500 to 1,000 eggs.
(b.2) Mulberry Leaves / Food Plants - Linkage to nearby plantations or provision of free saplings (20 plants).
(b.3) Disinfectants - Free disinfectant kit for the first season valued at Rs. 2,000.
(b.4) Packaging Material - Free cocoon storage bags provided.

(4) Market Linkage and Income Support
(a) Guaranteed Cocoon Purchase
(a.1) Buyers - State cocoon aggregation centers, private reeling units, and online auction platforms.
(a.2) Minimum Price Guarantee - Rs. 200–300 per kg for mulberry cocoons and Rs. 150–250 per kg for tassar cocoons, based on quality.
(a.3) Payment System - Payment is made through direct bank transfer within 7 days.
(a.4) Quality Testing - Free quality testing at collection centers with grading into A, B, and C categories for fair pricing.

(b) Women’s Producer Groups
(b.1) Group Size - 10–20 Resham Sakhis per village.
(b.2) Benefits - Collective marketing resulting in 5–10% higher prices, bulk input purchase, and shared technical support.
(b.3) Leadership Structure - One group leader is trained as a “Master Resham Sakhi”.

(c) Ongoing Technical Support
(c.1) Extension Officer Support - Monthly home visits during the first year and quarterly visits from the second year onwards.
(c.2) Helpline Facility - 24×7 toll-free sericulture helpline.
(c.3) Refresher Training - Free annual refresher training of 3 days.

(d) Financial Inclusion Support
(d.1) Bank Account Linkage - Mandatory Aadhaar-linked Jan Dhan bank account.
(d.2) Microfinance Access - NRLM linkage for expansion with loan support ranging from Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 2 lakh.
(d.3) Insurance Coverage - Crop insurance coverage of Rs. 10,000–20,000 per season.

(5) Income Potential
(a) Beginner Level - Space required is 100 sq. ft., with one batch per season.
Annual income ranges from Rs. 15,000 to Rs. 20,000 with approximately 2 hours of work per day.
(b) Regular Level - Space required is 150 sq. ft., with 3–4 batches per year.
Annual income ranges from Rs. 60,000 to Rs. 90,000 with 3–4 hours of work per day.
(c) Advanced Level - Space required is 200 sq. ft., with 5–6 batches per year.
Annual income ranges from Rs. 1,20,000 to Rs. 1,80,000 with 4–5 hours of work per day.
Eligibility:
(1) Primary Target Group - The primary target beneficiaries are rural women from Uttar Pradesh.
Land ownership is not required for eligibility.

(2) Basic Eligibility Criteria (All Conditions Must Be Met)
(a) Residency Requirement
(a.1) State Residency - The applicant must be a permanent resident of Uttar Pradesh.
(a.2) Area Preference - Preference is given to residents of rural areas.

(b) Age Criteria
(b.1) Minimum Age - The applicant must be at least 18 years old.
(b.2) Upper Age Limit - There is no upper age limit; however, preference is given to women aged 18–50 years.

(c) Required Documents
(c.1) Aadhaar Card - Mandatory for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) payments.
(c.2) Address Proof - Voter ID card or Ration Card is required as proof of residence.
(c.3) Bank Account - A valid bank account is required; Jan Dhan account is preferred.
(c.4) Photographs - Two passport-size photographs are required.

(d) First-Time Participation Condition
(d.1) Training and Subsidy History - The applicant must not have received sericulture training or subsidy under any previous scheme.

(e) Health and Physical Ability
(e.1) Physical Fitness - The applicant must be physically capable of handling silkworm rearing activities.
(e.2) Work Nature - The work involves light physical activity and does not require heavy lifting.

(3) Priority Categories (Selection Preference Order)
(a) SC/ST Women - Highest priority with a 40% reservation quota.
(b) OBC Women - Second priority with a 30% quota.
(c) Widows and Single Women - Third priority with a 25% quota.
(d) BPL / APL Rural Women - Fourth priority with a 20% quota.
(e) SHG Members - Additional preference of 15% for women who are members of Self-Help Groups.
(f) General Category - Remaining seats allocated under the balance quota.

(4) Who Cannot Apply (Exclusion Criteria)
(a) Employment Status - Government employees and pensioners are not eligible.
(b) Residence Status - Urban residents are not eligible, as the scheme is exclusively for rural women.
(c) Previous Sericulture Experience - Applicants already trained in sericulture under any scheme are not eligible.
(d) Gender Restriction - Men are not eligible, as this is a women-only scheme.
(e) State Residency - Non-Uttar Pradesh residents are not eligible.
(f) Existing Commercial Activity - Farmers already engaged in commercial sericulture operations are not eligible.

(5) Group Application through Self-Help Groups (SHGs)
(a) SHG Eligibility - Self-Help Groups with 10 or more women members can apply collectively.
(b) Group Coordination - A group leader is responsible for coordinating training and logistics.
(c) Shared Infrastructure - Common rearing spaces can be used by the group members.
(d) Collective Marketing - Group members benefit from collective marketing arrangements.

(6) Expected Application and Selection Statistics
(a) Annual Applications - Approximately 15,000–20,000 applications are expected every year.
(b) Selection Volume - Around 7,500 applicants are selected annually.
(c) Approval Rate - The overall approval rate is estimated at 35–40%.
